description.narrative: International Development Law Organization (IDLO) is a multilateral organisation with its head office in Rome dedicated to the promotion of rule of law. Sweden became a state member of IDLO in 2017. IDLO submitted a programme proposal to Sida - "Community Justice Programme in Uganda 2018-2023" - which has the main objective to enhance access to justice for women and men living in poverty, especially in the rural areas of Uganda. In concrete terms, the expected outcomes are: (1) Legal aid and empowerment of grassroots communities, (2) Strengthening capacities of and linkages between formal and informal justice systems, (3) Enhancing access to justice for women and girls, and (4) Improving the monitoring and accountability system within the Justice, Law and Order Sector (JLOS).The proposed Programme will focus on legally-empowering grassroots communities and enhancing the capacity of duty-bearers within the justice, law and order sector (JLOS) at the community level to provide the most vulnerable and marginalised citizens with quality legal knowledge, legal aid and other justice services to uphold their basic rights, challenge their grievances in an equitable manner, and obtain effective justice remedy and reparation or compensation from both formal and informal justice mechanisms. The Programme is grounded in the appreciation that accessibility of quality, affordable and fair justice services, or provision of legal assistance in Uganda remains challenging due to a number of factors, with disputes not resolved by formal justice institutions in a timely and equitable manner. The Programme has been a result of a two-year multi-stakeholder consultative process, ensuring endorsement and buy-in from key actors, including the Government, local communities, civil society, academia and relevant development partners. IDLO's mission is to enable governments, empower people, and to strengthen institutions to realise justice, peace and sustainable devlopment. The IDLO programme in Uganda will therefore build strong collaborations with governments (JLOS), intergovernmental organisations, and civil society groups by providing technical assistance, support capacity development, generate knowledge and advocate for policy change in Uganda. Capacity building of IDLO implementing partners will an integral part of the programme. The capacity of the duty bearers´ to fulfill their responsibilities and rightsholders´abilities to demand accountability and access to justice are both equally important parts of the programme. The financing provided by Sweden shall be deposited by IDLO in a SEK non-interest-bearing bank account. This is because IDLO is an inter-governmental not-for-profit organisation.Financial support for implementation of programmatic activities will be through both the Justice Law and Order Sector (JLOS) with IDLO supporting selected agreed activities within JLOS institutions and support to Non-State Institutions through a sub grant making process. IDLO will support up to 20 sub-grantees financially, and provide capacity building for management of funds and program implementation. The number of sub-grantees will be phased over the duration of programme implementation. An initial number of no more than 5 sub-grantees, will be directly selected for the first year of implementation. The selection and assessment of Implementing Partners will be carried out by IDLO in accordance with its applicable regulations, rules, policies and procedures.

International Development Law Organization (IDLO) är en multilateral organisation med säte i Rom med huvudsyfte att främja rättssäkerhet. Sverige blev medlem i IDLO 2017.
IDLO inkom till Sida med ett programförslag – ”Community Justice in Uganda 2018-2023” – med huvudmålet att förbättra tillgång till rättvisa för kvinnor och män i fattigdom, framförallt på landsbygden i Uganda. Konkret är de förväntade resultaten:
(1)Rättshjälp och stärkande av gräsrotsamhällen, (2)Stärka kapaciteten av och länken mellan formella och informella rättssystem, (3)Öka tillgång till rättvisa för kvinnor och flickor, och (4)Förbättra uppföljnings- och ansvarsutkrävandesystem inom rättssektorn (Justice, Law and Order Sector, JLOS)
Det föreslagna programmet kommer fokusera på att juridiskt stärka lokalbefolkning (på bynivå) och öka kapaciteten hos aktörer inom rättssektorn (JLOS) på lokal nivå för att förse de mest utsatta och marginaliserade invånarna med juridisk kunskap, rättshjälp och andra rättstjänster av god kvalitet för att upprätthålla deras grundläggande rättigheter, omhänderta deras klagomål på ett rättvist sätt och få till effektiva rättsåtgärder och gottgörelse eller ersättning från både de formella och informella rättssystemen. Programmet grundar sig i förståelsen att tillgång till prisvärda och rättvisa rättstjänster av god kvalité och tillhandahållande av rättshjälp fortfarande är en utmaning på grund av ett antal faktorer, med tvister som inte löses inom det formella rättssystemet på ett rättvist sätt. Programmet är ett resultat av en två-årig process där flera intressenter varit inblandade, för att säkerställa godkännande och stöd från nyckelaktörer; inkluderande regeringen, lokalsamhällen, det civila samhället, akademin och relevanta utvecklingspartners.
IDLO:s uppdrag är att stärka människor, regeringar och institutioner för att uppnå rättvisa, fred och hållbar utveckling. IDLO kommer därför att bygga starka samarbetem med myndigheter inom framför allt rättssäktorn (JLOS), mellanstatliga organisationer och civilsamhällesorganisationer genom att tillandahålla tekniskt stöd, stödja kapacitetsutveckling, generera ny kunskap och förespråka policyförändringar i Uganda. Kapacitetsutveckling av IDLO:s partner är en integrerad del av programmet. Kapaciteten hos ansvarsbärare att uppfylla sina skyldigheter och rättighetsbärares förmåga att utkräva ansvar och tillgång till rättvisa är lika viktiga delar i programmet.
Finansieringen är på 152,5 MSEK för åren 2018 till 2023 och programmets längd beräknas vara 5 år, med start i December 2018.
IDLO ska hålla finansieringen från Sverige på ett icke-räntebärande SEK-konto, eftersom det är en icke-vinstdrivande multilateral organisation.
Finansiellt stöd för implementeringen av programaktiviteter kommer ske både genom rättssektorn (JLOS), där IDLO som stödjer ett urval avtalade aktiviteter inom JLOS-institutioner, och genom stöd till icke-statliga institutioner via en vidareförmedlingsstruktur. IDLO kommer stödja upp till 20 vidareförmedlande mottagare finansiellt och tillhandahålla kapacitetsuppbyggnad inom finansiell styrning, redovisning och programimplementering. Antalet implementerande tredje parter till vilka IDLO ska vidareförmedla medel är tänkt att gradvis öka under programmets genomförande. Ett initialt antal på högst 5 vidareförmedlande mottagare kommer väljas för det första implementeringsåret. Urvalet och bedömningen av implementerande partner ska utföras av IDLO i enlighet med deras applicerbara regler, policies och procedurer.
IDLO kommer att genomföra programmet i Uganda genom sitt lokala kontor (benämnt "Programme Management Team") som består av personal i Kampala, med stöd av IDLO:s regionala Afrikakontor i Nairobi, liksom IDLO:s huvudkontor i Rom, och IDLO:s filialkontor i Haag, Nederländerna.
Sidas fokalpunkt för IDLO har informerat UD FMR om det föreslagna stödet till programmet i Uganda i enlighet med vad som stadgas i regeringens strategi för samarbete med multilaterala organisationer (se ärende 14/000743).

During the reporting period (January-December 2023), the programme implemented several activities and attained the following results;
Enhanced access to justice for vulnerable communities in hard-to-reach areas:10,381 (F: 5,503; M: 4,878) persons accessed legal assistance with 2,097 (F: 1,493; M: 604) through programme interventions implemented by IDLOs partners namely; Centre for Food and Adequate Living Rights (CEFROHT), FIDA-Uganda, ULS, Justice Centres Uganda (JCU), Law Development Centre-Legal Aid Clinic (LDC-LAC), Penal Reform International (PRI) and World Voices Uganda (WVU). All the beneficiaries were able to resolve their legal issues within three (3) months of contact with an implementing partner, compared to the average 177 days it took to resolve a case in the courts during FY 2022/23.
Through the above mentioned legal assistance, 16 acres of land and UGX 46,236,000 equivalent to EUR 11,007; SEK 122,232) were recovered for the beneficiaries.
Improved oversight in case management and reduced case backlog at the High Court level: Through the programme, the Judiciary Case Backlog Monitoring Committee (CBMC) continued to hold quarterly performance reviews of the High Court Divisions and Circuits. This exercise enabled the Judiciary leadership to set targets, track progress and implement the adopted case management strategies aimed at improving case disposal. The review meetings also encouraged accountability and satisfactory performance among the Divisions and Circuits, hence improving efficiency in justice service delivery. For example, the case completion rate at the Commercial Division increased by 13.1% in the third quarter, which is from 1,065 cases as of 31 December 2022 to 1,226 cases on 31 March 2023. This increase alone unlocked UGX 11,744,026,291.66 (equivalent EUR 2,754,963.19; SEK 30,733,438) into the Uganda economy.
At the Civil and Land Divisions of the High Court, by the end of FY 2022/23, only 42,960 (27.48%) of the pending caseload of 156,349 cases in the courts were backlog. This indicated a 4.52% reduction compared to the previous FY when case backlog constituted 32% of the entire caseload. The Criminal Division also registered an increase in its case disposal rate, from 1,838 cases as of 31December 2022 to 1,935 at the end of March 2023. The case backlog at the Family Division reduced by 8% from 1,320 cases in December 2022 to 1,212 at the end of March 2023.
As a result, the performance of High Court Divisions and Circuits greatly improved with speedy case disposal and case backlog reduction. Specifically, in the Financial Year (FY)2022/23, the time taken to dispose of a case by the Judiciary improved by almost six (6) months (177) days compared to FY 2021/22. This was reflected by the courts completion of 266,333 cases out of a total case load of 422,672 cases - a summation of cases brought forward from FY 2021/22 and those registered in FY 2022/23.
Strengthened linkages between formal and informal justice mechanisms through establishment of legislative and policy frameworks: The Judiciary, in collaboration with the Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (MoJCA) with support from the CJP developed a draft national Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Policy and an Alternative Justice strategy (AJS) to strengthen linkages between ADR and formal judicial processes. The AJS ws launched during the first The Implementation of the AJS Strategy by the Judiciary was rolled out and it is expected to, among others: (i) serve as a case backlog reduction/caseload management measure; (ii) provide for and support existing Judiciary ADR mechanisms and the inclusion or incorporation of traditional approaches and institutions; (iii) localize justice solutions and delivery to inculcate an ownership principle, with users of AJS pathways and processes embracing them as their own in resolving their disputes; and (iv) create a framework that promotes ADR as a vehicle for timely resolution of disputes while preserving critical relationships. Implementation of the national ADR Policy awaits adoption by the Cabinet. The ADR Policy will be the foundation of a legal framework for all forms of ADR in Uganda.
Increased commitment and buy-in among district actors to promote access to justice for vulnerable persons at the local level: Through out the reporting period, District local governments in CJP implementation areas showed commitment towards enhancing access to justice by ensuring continued provision of legal aid and information services to persons affected by injustices in these areas. In three districts (Iganga, Lira and Wakiso), the District Local Governments offered free office space to FIDA-Uganda to establish legal aid clinics. Additionally, free radio time and transportation of legal officers was given by district actors to ensure continued sensitization of communities on their rights and available support services. Moreover, to sustain efforts to prevent and respond to SGBV in Butaleja district, the District Local Government embarked on dissemination of the ordinance addressing teenage pregnancies and early marriage among actors and communities.
IDLO reported an unforeseen achievement of improving women's livelihoods through skills enhancement and registration of 11 income generating groups. IDLOs implementing partner, FIDA-Uganda , in collaboration with relevant district structures such as the agriculture and production departments of the Iganga District Local Government, equipped 240 women with diverse income generating skills including soap making and small scale farming. This was to enhance their capacity to generate income for themselves and their families. Upon mastering the skills, the women formed 11 groups. Through the Community Justice Programme, FIDA-Uganda assisted the women groups to register with the district authorities as Community- Based Organizations (CBOs). One of the groups used its registration certificate to acquire a loan of UGX 200,000 (approximately EUR 48; SEK 529) and boosted their liquid soap making business. Overtime, with the profit acquired, two (2) group members constructed decent housing for their families while other group members were able to pay school fees and other necessities for their children.
The Embassy also noted that besides providing outcomes from activity implementation during the activity period, IDLO also assessed the impact/contribution of the programme to the overall justice context. IDLO reported that because of the Community Justice Programme there has been;
a) an increase in the number of cases finalized in the courts by supporting the case backlog strategy of the judiciary. Specifically, in the Financial Year (FY) 2022/23, the time taken to dispose of a case by the Judiciary improved by almost six (6) months (177) days compared to FY 2021/22. An Improved case disposal rate was also registered from 55% in 2022 to 63% in 2023 and backlog reduction from 51,748 (32% in 2021) to 42,960 (27.5 in 2023).
b) a strengthened Alternative Dispute Resolution framework, through the development of the draft ADR Policy and the operationalisation of the Alternative Justice Strategy.
c) an enhanced case monitoring system, through the development of mechanisms and tools to track performance of courts and case management by the Judiciary Case backlog Committee.
d) an enhanced gender responsiveness in the criminal justice system through the adoption of alternative non-custodial sentencing by the Judiciary for women offenders and community driven solutions in the prevention and response to Sexual and Gender-Based Violence (SGBV).
It is particularly encouraging to see the contribution that the programme is making towards addressing case backlog and court performance in the high courts and how this is impacting on the overall statistics on case backlog at national level as illustrated above. This result is directly attributable to the programme since it is only the CJP that is funding the Judiciary Case backlog Committee and its meetings which design strategies, set targets, and assess performance of judges.
